clusters.name: Your grandfather Gordon's death, 1991–1994
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Gordon's death in June 1991, over the next few years: your wrist injury stopped your playing and left you anxious and lower in functioning; you and Rafe clashed and he moved out; you were on your own, getting high, absorbed in radios; you felt lost and low, unable to get going, with your grandfather gone and your mother about to remarry; your grandmother Winifred had thyroid surgery; you drifted through a bleak year at community college, nights out playing pool and days asleep. By early 1994 an exchange in Lisbon and Porto brought your drive back, and you tore through the rest of your degree. Your father and grandfather Clifford's reunion and your move to the rebuilt Hollin Road house sit close by, but the shifts centre on your own loss of footing after the death and your slow climb back.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Winifred's bowel cancer diagnosis, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Winifred being found to have bowel cancer in 2001 or 2002, within the next two years: you ran out of steam for performing and felt less content by the month, your anxiety rose and functioning fell; you had a disastrous audition for the national orchestra and were done with performing; you were on poor terms with family and friends; you left Thornbury for Gull Harbour, then met Marisol and moved to Fenwick, and when you split that winter you sank into a deep depression. You could not face your family; your parents seemed a world away. You relied on friends instead, and your father and friend Corbin spoke several times during your stay. By early 2004 you returned to your therapist and began swimming, and your functioning began to climb; your grandmother died in February. The period holds your own collapse and slow recovery alongside hers, with your move away and the failed relationship as the family's reactions piled up.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Lorna's death, 2008–2010
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Lorna's death in January 2008, within a couple of years: you were too drained for conversation with your mother and withdrew from her; she pressed you to visit at Alder Creek and your anxiety rose; you kept the door shut on her when she came; you stopped speaking to your mother when you moved to Marlow Sound for nursing school that summer, a silence that held for roughly a year. Your aunt Imogen had a stroke with months of rehabilitation. Your partner's brother Leo's two children were born. The period sits around your cutoff from your mother, which held hard after the lodge visit, and only eased once you returned home in 2013.

clusters.name: Your marriage to Wren, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: Around your marriage to Wren in March 2017, within the next two years: you saw your mother a bit less once Wren came along; your cousin Alice was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis; your sister Tara flew for an airline and married; your aunt Imogen lashed out when muddled and had not been like that before; your job steadied and paid well, easing your anxiety, but you constantly felt you ought to be driving projects forward, your normal anxious state; you started a sleeping pill; you aimed for shorter, more regular calls with your mother; your sister was expecting her first child. In October 2019, your partner was swamped with events one after another, and you overfunctioned laying out a plan to settle her; she talks with her father and brother all day, nothing happens to one that the others don't hear; she settled once the weekend had a plan. You awoke from the small hours at the lake house for her mother's retirement, could not get back to sleep, and felt you didn't belong; your partner grew anxious when you'd had no sleep at family occasions. The period holds the shifts in your household and Wren's family around the marriage, with your own sleep troubles and her family's closeness running alongside.

periods.name: the year I left home
periods.words: The first is the year I left home: I went off to the conservatory, hurt my wrist in the first term and couldn't play, dropped out and drifted at my mother's place, then spent a bleak spell at the community college shooting pool every night until an exchange in Portugal snapped me out of it and I tore through the rest of my coursework.

periods.name: the long slump
periods.words: The second is the long slump, roughly ages 27 to 29, when nothing at home felt right, I moved to Gull Harbour away from nearly everyone I knew, then followed Marisol to Fenwick, and when that fell apart I went under, a depression I only really climbed out of after nursing school.
